cards.text: Jesus has just come down the mountain with His twelve new apostles, and a huge crowd is pushing in just to touch Him (Luke 6:13-19). He looks up at His disciples and says, “Blessed are you who are poor,” and friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer owning nothing but dust. So I am LEANING in.

cards.question: Jesus calls the poor blessed. What reason does He give them?

answers.text: Yours is the kingdom of God

cards.text: Next: “Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled.” Hungry NOW, filled LATER, like every baker who ever stood in front of my oven staring at the timer.

cards.question: Jesus flips it the same way for the ones who weep now. He calls them blessed and says they will ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus calls you blessed even when people hate you, shut you out, insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man, which is how Jesus talks about Himself. That's not getting left out of the group chat, friend, that's getting left out AND talked about in it.

cards.question: When people hate them because of the Son of Man, what does Jesus tell His disciples to do in that day?
True or false: Jesus says the reward for being hated because of the Son of Man will come here on earth.

cards.text: And Jesus says the fathers of the ones doing the hating treated the prophets in the same way. Friend, getting treated like the prophets puts you in a club with some VERY famous members.
Then Jesus flips the whole sermon like a cookie on a spatula: “But woe to you who are rich,” and friend, I'm standing on a GOLD base. I'm sweating.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the rich have already received their comfort.

cards.text: “Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger.” Same flip as the blessings, just running the other direction.

cards.question: Jesus has a woe for the ones who laugh now too. What does He say will happen to them?

cards.text: One more woe, and this one isn't about money, food or laughing. Friend, I'm already sweating on my gold base, and He is NOT done.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says woe to you when all men speak well of you.
The hated ones got treated like the prophets. For the ones everybody praises, Jesus says their fathers treated the ___ prophets in the same way.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, “But to those of you who will listen, I say:” and He's about to talk about enemies. Friend, when somebody opens like THAT, you put the cookie down and lean in.

cards.question: What does Jesus tell the listeners to do about their enemies?

cards.text: Then He adds: do good to those who hate you. To the ones who HATE you? Friend, I've been a cookie stamper my whole life, and I have never been pressed this hard.

cards.question: Jesus keeps the same pattern going: ___ those who curse you.

cards.text: And pray for those who mistreat you. Then Jesus gets personal: someone strikes you on one cheek.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says if someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also.

cards.text: If someone takes your cloak, don't hold back your tunic, and give to everyone who asks you. So if somebody takes my apron, I offer up the HAT, and friend, that hat is half my height.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says if anyone takes what is yours, demand it back.

cards.text: Then Jesus gives one line about how to treat people, and it's one you've probably heard your whole life.

cards.question: What's the line Jesus gives about how to treat others?

answers.text: Do to others as you would have them do to you
Treat others the way that they treat you
Do good to others when they have earned it

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, “If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you?” Friend, I loved the people who loved me back for YEARS and thought I deserved a medal.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says even sinners love those who love them.

cards.text: Same goes for doing good to people who do good to you, and lending where you expect to be repaid, because even sinners do that. Lending to somebody who'll pay you back in full isn't generosity, friend, it's just a bank wearing an apron.

cards.question: So Jesus says to love your enemies, do good to them and lend to them, expecting ___ in return.
Jesus says then their reward will be great, and they'll be sons of the Most High. What does He say the Most High is like?

answers.text: He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked
He rewards the ones who have earned it
He blesses the ones who bless Him

cards.text: “Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.” Then quick ones: do not judge, and you will not be judged, and do not condemn, and you will not be condemned.

cards.question: Same pattern one more time: Jesus says if you forgive, you will be ___.

cards.text: Give, and it will be given to you: a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, poured into your lap. Friend, that's how I pack a cookie box, and the lid has NEVER closed.

cards.question: Jesus gives one last reason to give so freely. What is it?

answers.text: The measure you use will be measured back to you
Whatever you hold on to will be taken away
Your giving will be seen and praised by others

cards.text: And that's where we'll set the timer for now. Jesus isn't done teaching yet, friend, so keep that apron on.
